_README: Venues verified by hand against a named public source, used ahead of every other
venue source. This file exists for two reasons.
1. It replaces data/stadiums-src.csv, whose licence we were never able to establish.
Nothing in the build reads that csv any more.
2. Wikidata lists historic home grounds alongside current ones with no way to tell
them apart in our extract, so the resolver correctly refuses a club with more
than one. These are those clubs, resolved by checking which ground is current.
'venue_country' is only set where the ground stands in a different country from the
league the club plays in. It is what the land check tests against; 'country' stays
the league's country so the club still appears under the right national filter.
Adding an entry means checking a source and naming it in 'checked'. Do not copy a
coordinate out of a search result without opening the page it came from.

venues.checked: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_Palace_F.C. - home ground since 1924. Wikidata also lists Crystal Palace Park, which is the pre-1915 site.

en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Louis_II gives the address but no coordinate; 43 deg 43'39"N 7 deg 24'56"E agreed by three independent sources. Monaco is not in the Wikidata country list, so the club had no row at all.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_FC - moved to Jean-Bouin in 2025. BOTH Wikidata rows (Stade Charlety, Stade Robert Bobin) are out of date; either would have been a confident wrong pin.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich - moved 2005. Single unambiguous Wikidata row; it was the English/German name difference that lost the match.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SC_Freiburg - moved 2021. Wikidata also lists Dreisamstadion (1954-2021) and Moeslestadion.

en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSG_1899_Hoffenheim - moved 2009. Wikidata also lists Dietmar-Hopp-Stadion, which the women's team still uses. Ground has carried several sponsor names (Rhein-Neckar-Arena, SNP Arena).
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.C._Braga - home since 2003. Single unambiguous Wikidata row; lost on the name only.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deportivo_de_La_Coruña - Abanca-Riazor. Single unambiguous Wikidata row; lost on the name only.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rheinpark_Stadion. Liechtenstein is not in the Wikidata country list, so the club fell back to a city-centre pin.
